entries.note: DOI resolves to Wernig 2008 Cancer Cell (PMID 18394554); quote is a verbatim truncation of the abstract's last sentence. Opening untested at 2008 is correct; FDA review restates the 60/120 mg/kg STAT3/5 blockade.

Pardanani 2011 JCO (PMID 21220608) abstract quote verbatim; NCT00631462 has no results. Same/direction_only fair. Caveat: NS-018 phase 1 reported allele burden 'largely unchanged' and BMS-911543 mice showed no allele fall; neither changes this fedratinib entry.
Quote verbatim in Wernig abstract. No human exposure target or margin from the mouse; FDA review shows FIH dose set by escalation (MTD 680 mg/d). untested/no_prediction correct.
Quote verbatim in Wernig 2008 abstract. Model is the one the FDA review cites for efficacy (lines ~314-319 of the CDTL review). Opening untested 2008 correct.

Pardanani 2015 JAMA Oncol (PMID 26181658) quote verbatim; primary endpoint SVR35. NCT01437787 results first posted 2026-08-11, NCT01423851 2022-03-09, NCT01236352 2019-05-21 all confirmed. Pairing; same direction_only supported.

Bundle text line 327 has the quote verbatim, but the next sentence reads 'Gait abnormalities were also observed in high-dose animals' - worth recording in the note. IND October 2007 confirmed (line 125); target organs marrow/liver (rat), many in dog.
Quote verbatim in Wernig 2008 abstract. untested opening entry on the mouse track is correct.

Verstovsek 2017 Leukemia (PMID 27479177, epub 2016-08) quote verbatim; Nakaya 2014 BCJ model quote verbatim and explicitly predicts 'reduced hematologic adverse effects'. Contra supported, though 'reduced' vs other JAK2i could be read as partial.

Quote verbatim in bundle (line 2624); review also gives the 0.3-fold AUC rat thiamine study and ThTr inhibition. Contra on tox track 2019 supported; rat gait abnormalities at high dose is a weak CNS hint, not encephalopathy.
Geron 2008 Cancer Cell abstract (PMID 18394555) carries the quote verbatim; STAT5 inhibition in PV progenitors, no human pSTAT then. Opening untested at first use 2008, class level, correct.

Label 2019 line 570 verbatim. Model (2008) preceded patient readout, so same not retro; direction_only for pSTAT5 vs pSTAT3 is right. Pardanani 2011 JCO full text may report pSTAT3 earlier (year 2011); not retrieved.
Quote is the last sentence of the Geron 2008 abstract, verbatim; prospective (phase 1 results 2011), untested 2008 correct. Cells were PV progenitors, as the note says.

JAKARTA JAMA Oncol 2015 abstract (PMID 26181658) verbatim; primary spleen endpoint met, model predated it, same is right. Phase 1 (Pardanani 2011) had 39% spleen response earlier, but phase 3 primary endpoint is the right gate.
Zhang 2014 DMD abstract (PMID 25063672) verbatim; opens citing the terminated program for WE, so built post hoc. Opening untested 2014 acceptable.
Abstract verbatim; potent Caco-2/hTHTR2 inhibition reproduced the known WE mechanism after the clinic knew it: retrodiction true, status retro (not same), 2014 correct.

FDA multidiscipline review (bundle txt l.2776-2778) verbatim; study OPT-2017-097 run 'because of claims that cases of Wernicke's encephalopathy occurred'. Year 2017 is a study-code proxy; untested opening fine.

Review l.2628/2779 verbatim. Post-hoc assay showed only weak ThTr inhibition at ~100x Cmax, failing to reproduce WE; failed retrodiction is contra under the brief. Low confidence apt given disputed causality and Zhang 2014 disagreement.

missing: In-vitro thiamine-transport model (Caco-2 cells, recombinant hTHTR2): Zhang et al. 2014 Drug Metab Dispos, doi:10.1124/dmd.114.058883 (PMID 25063672) showed fedratinib inhibits thiamine uptake after the WE cases - a safety track, retrodiction: true, status retro (2014); the FDA review restates the ThTr1/ThTr2 assay (24.5%/44.2% at 300 uM).

Patient-derived JAK2V617F+ progenitor colony and xenograft model: Geron et al. 2008 Cancer Cell, doi:10.1016/j.ccr.2008.02.017 (PMID 18394555), TG101348 inhibited patient progenitor colonies and engraftment - an ex_vivo efficacy/engagement track (PV-derived cells) with no entry; BMS-911543 also inhibited CD34+ cells from JAK2V617F patients (cited in Pomicter 2015).

BMS-911543 on the same JAK2V617F BMT mouse track: Pomicter et al. 2015 Exp Hematol, doi:10.1016/j.exphem.2015.03.006 (PMID 25912019) found 'limited activity', no RBC effect and no allele-burden fall; NCT01236352 lists IWG best overall response as a PRIMARY outcome (results posted 2019-05-21), and Tefferi 2023 BCJ doi:10.1038/s41408-022-00780-9 reports 62% spleen response in 31 Mayo BMS-911543 patients. The draft's 'not scored/unsettled' needs an explicit entry or note.

BMS-911543 on JAK2V617F+ patient CD34+ progenitors (Purandare et al. 2012 Leukemia 26:280, cited by Pomicter 2015; DOI not verified): a member drug's run on the same ex-vivo progenitor system, could be an entry on track jak2v617f-patient-progenitor-colony; its trial outcome is a business stop.
rule_questions: BMS-911543: the mouse predicted limited activity (Pomicter 2015); NCT01236352 has IWG best overall response as a co-primary (3 PR/42 per draft) while a Mayo cohort reports 62% spleen response. Is this neg/same (limited model, limited IWG response, program stopped for business) or contra (patients' spleens responded) or unsettled because the stop was a business decision?

Fedratinib (Wernig, Gilliland lab) and NS-018 (Nakaya, Nippon Shinyaku) and BMS-911543 (Pomicter) used separately built JAK2V617F retroviral BMT mice; does 'one system' mean one model type (one model_id, as drafted) or one lab's system?

Should the rat/dog toxicology track carry a dose-cell entry (untested, unpublished) since its data set the FIH start but were public only in 2019, or is the dose cell correctly limited to the mouse track?

Safety contra for Wernicke's: the post-hoc rat thiamine study reached only 0.3x human AUC, and rodent chow is thiamine-replete - is WE a harm 'the species could have shown' at the exposures the tox package used?
